author: Golden Gate Media
title: Truck driver hurls big rig off California interstate; Cops accuse him of being six-times over limit
text:
11 hours ago A commercial truck driver in Tracy was arrested for driving under the influence after veering off the roadway and crashing into a field, according to the California Highway Patrol. Authorities say the incident could have ended far worse, but no injuries were reported.
Photo by CHP Investigators with CHP’s Tracy office said the driver was operating the big rig at nearly three times the legal blood alcohol concentration limit for a passenger vehicle—far exceeding the stricter threshold required for commercial drivers. The crash left the fully loaded truck off the roadway, raising serious concerns about the dangers posed by impaired driving behind the wheel of heavy-duty vehicles.
Officials emphasized that the weight and size of a commercial truck significantly increase the risk of catastrophic damage when something goes wrong. A big rig, often carrying thousands of pounds, can quickly become a deadly hazard if not operated safely and responsibly.
“SIX TIMES over the Commercial BAC limit 🚛❌🍺 Not exactly the delivery anyone ordered,” CHP Tracy said in a statement. “A commercial driver left the roadway and ended up in a field. Thankfully, no one was hurt—but the reason behind it is serious.”
“The driver was contacted and arrested for DUI, operating at nearly THREE TIMES the legal limit for a passenger vehicle—and well beyond the stricter limit for commercial drivers,” the agency added.
CHP is using the incident as a reminder that impaired driving—especially in commercial vehicles—can have devastating consequences. “No load, deadline, or excuse is worth driving impaired. Drive sober. Stay alert. Arrive alive.”
